title: ERS-EO ALPSTAR FEDERATED LAYER DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY IMPLEMENTATION (ACTIVITY 2B)
description: Activity 2B addresses Phase B of the Alpstar Federation Layer, aiming to consolidate requirements, architecture, and prototype validation for a federated, multi stakeholder space system. Building on the MRD 2.0, this phase will define and specify all functional, technical, and security requirements of the Federation Layer, including secure interfaces with commercial service providers and Alpstar Nodes via unidirectional "diode" connections.The activity encompasses the full design of the Alpstar system architecture and the development and demonstration of a User Ground Segment prototype. Comprehensive specifications will be produced for all major Federation Layer components, ensuring interoperability, security, and scalability across federated participants.The procurement also includes the acquisition of a minimum of three months of satellite data, necessary to support validation and testing of the Ground Segment prototype under operationally representative conditions.A key deliverable of this phase is a User Ground Segment prototype featuring:A role based user interface, enabling differentiated access and operational views.An initial implementation of the Digital Governance Agent (DGA), enforcing a first set of provisional federation rules and acting as the central mission management and planning capability.The Alpstar Federated Layer shall integrate the following core functionalities:Digital Governance Agent (DGA)for federation rule enforcement and central mission managementSecure Data Pooling Service for controlled dissemination of observation resultsFederated Ledger to record and audit transactionsStandardised APIs interfacing with Nodes (FOS and PDGS)Federated Data Lake hosted in a cloud environmentVirtual Constellation Management for coordinated asset utilisationFederated CatalogueCross federation taskingNATO FMN / Joint ISR tasking interfaces routed to AlpstarRole based user interfaceFederation dashboard for operational and governance oversightWith a target duration of 12 months, the expected outcomes of Activity 2B include:Complete specifications of the Federation LayerDefinition of the Federation Layer architectureRough Order of Magnitude (ROM)cost estimate for implementationIdentification of the industrial consortiumDevelopment plan and integrated scheduleDemonstration of the User Ground Segment prototypeThis phase will provide the technical, architectural, and organisational foundations required to progress Alpstar toward a fully operational, secure, and governed federated space capability.

title: POWER EFFICIENT USER PLANE FUNCTIONS FOR B5G SMALL SATELLITE PLATFORMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.016)
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to develop and test a power efficient 5G User Plane Function (UPF) prototype, implemented onto space enabled hardware platforms. The development will leverage concrete laboratory results of various RAN splits and compensate for their impact on the 5G protocol stack. Finally, system integration with a ground segment control plane will be tested, over emulated LEO constellationsTargeted Improvements:- At least 50 % power consumption reduction when compared to terrestrial 5G user plane deployments.- Reduced user plane latency.- Reduced control plane signalling.- Device to device communications over 5G-enable satellite payloads. - Develop a 5G user plane prototype on space enabled hardware.Description:Amongst all, regenerative payloads could provide delay sensitive communications, neutral hosting services for cross-border service continuation, store and forward operations, and connectivity among two or more 5G User Equipment (UE) devices for emergency response and disaster relief services. Due to their low cost and short production cycles, small satellites are attractive to host 5G enabled payloads. In contrast to terrestrial 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core Network (CN) deployments, on board payloads are bound to stringent power, and mass constraints imposed by the platform. As an example, a typical microsatellite can support an average of 100W power for pure payload operations, whereas a typical 5G terrestrial network, can consume over 2000W assuming high availability within a virtualised network infrastructure. It is apparent that to fit a 5G payload under these rigorous restrictions, a high degree of optimisation is required to current RAN and CN deployments. Currently, there are various options being considered within the NTN community, to shape the on boardB5G regenerative payload. However, there are no studies with respect to power consumption, signalling overhead and standardisation impact of these options. This activity will develop a modified 5G RAN protocol stack and user plane functions to reduce the latencyand power consumption by 50%. This will include signalling reduction techniques over the N2 and Xn interfaces, between the on-board user plane and ground segment control plane infrastructure as well as traffic influencing to steer non-critical traffic. A UPF prototype will be designed, manufactured. Testing will include device-to-device communication (unicast, multicast and broadcast) over emulated LEO constellations. Outputs of this activity shall be available to standardisation bodies.
